posts.body:
It's a new year, which means it's time for a new event!
"I Love you, ___!" Game Jam
Art by
@Archeia
​
We all have our favorite default characters from RPG Maker, so now it's time to show that love! Pick your favorite default character and make a short game with them as the main character. Highlight the reasons why you love this RPG Maker character, and give other people a reason to love them too!
Love XP's Alex? Let him be the hero of a dungeon crawler!
Want some more of MZ's Priscilla? Have her help out on a farm!
Think MV's chicken is overlooked? Make it the star of a short visual novel!
Use any RPG Maker engine sold in the Komodo store to create your game and let your favorite character stand in the spotlight!
Deadline:
February 14th, 11:59PM EST (4:59AM UTC)
Reward:
Everyone who submits a game will receive the 'RM Love' participation badge!
Those who made a game with just base engine resources and without scripts/plugins will receive the 'RTP Hero' badge!
Rules:
This is an
RTP-only event
, so you may only use the resources that come with RPG Maker. You can use resources from one engine in another (such as XP sprite and tiles in MZ), but no edits beyond adjusted the resources to work in the engine are allowed
Sprites generated with Ace/MV/MZ's base generator may be used, but should not be the focus of the game. No added pieces should be used, so make sure that you're only using the generator parts that come with the base engine
Scripts/plugins
may
be used, but will mean you won't get the 'RTP Hero' badge
The scripts/plugins should not add extra resources to the game (so a keybind plugin is okay, a plugin that requires images to make a new menu is not)
Games should be between 5-30 minutes long
All other forum rules about games are still in effect
If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
The
submission thread
is now up, so please submit your games there.

The problem with MIDI is that it's just the performance data. Midi by itself has no sound. It relies on either the midi sound libraries built into your operating system, or external sound libraries.
So... Not to be the pedantic a/shole but any version converted from midi to mp3 is *technically * an alternate version. What I mean is that there isn't a "standardized timbre".  So, for a example:
If I listen to BYOB from System of a Down, it's also going to have Serj Tankian singing.
If I listen to a MIDI, on one system it might Rick Astley singing. On a different system it might be Korn singing.
Note that this was just a funny example. MIDI does not do vocals, only instrument data.

@StarWolff
- As the typo in the title itself shows, this one is rife with typos. It also has no balance whatsoever (not that I'm really qualified to speak on that). There's a heal skill, but you can only use it in battle. Enemies don't drop items. (I managed to get a potion once, somehow, and that's it.) There seems to be no way to restore MP (unless it's an item that never dropped for me), so I had to fight the final boss with just 15 MP left. The maps are weird and uninspiring (no, this is not because it's RTP).
I Love You, Ptook by
@wingkowati
– Good use of some of the SceneX BGM tracks (at least, I'm pretty sure that's what they were, didn't explicitly check) and the tint function. The, uhh… plot? Can I call it that? It was decently funny, whatever you want to call it. I didn't much like how random tiles were just impassable for no reason though. (Side note: I don't know why the chicken went for the pork instead of the fruit.) Oh, but one big mistake: a king is referred to as "Your Majesty", not "Your Highness". (There were other typos too, mainly randomly-capitalized words, but that one was particularly egregious to me.)
I Love Banner by
@TheAM-Dol
– Major negative points for trying to force me into fullscreen at launch. Then when pressing F4 to go back to windowed mode, the window wasn't even the right size and I had to resize to see everything, somehow? The character selection menu was a really cool trick though… but you should've disabled menu access, because attempting to access the menu crashed the game. There were quite a few typos here as well. For what it's worth, I did
not
play the "Enshtified" version. Given the fullscreen complaints, maybe I should have.
Kitty's Day by
@Midona018
– It asks for 3 carrots and a potato. There's a carrot literally sitting on the counter 2 tiles over that you can't take. Why? Then after re-entering the house, I can't leave because I'm already standing on the exit tile (need to step off and back). This same problem seems to plague all the map transitions, though it's slightly less bad when the transition is wider. And you can take infinite flour, seemingly? This one is also rife with spelling and grammar errors. That said, on the whole, I liked this one – it sort of felt similar to the Blanchette one I played earlier, though it wasn't as long.
Slime vs Escape Room by
@Pixelbird14
– This one was pretty decent. It wasn't especially challenging or anything but I thought it was pretty well put together.
Reid's Way Home from the Desert by

– This was a pretty good example of how you can make a game that's not even remotely an RPG with the engine. I managed to get 113 points before Game Over. No idea if that's good or not.
